reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific mechanistic claims about diffusion, segregation, and oxidation behavior in HEAs, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific claim that high configurational entropy enhances diffusion-driven surface segregation of reactive elements to improve oxidation resistance relative to conventional alloys.
premises: High configurational entropy enhances atomic diffusion in HEAs
Enhanced diffusion leads to preferential surface segregation of reactive elements (Cr, Al, Si)
Segregated reactive elements rapidly oxidize to form a continuous, adherent protective oxide layer
This mechanism is specific to high-entropy alloys and not conventional alloys with similar reactive element content
The effect is operative under high-temperature oxidation conditions (>800°C) with sufficient reactive elements (>15%)
